recommendation: Keep the human-review audit. If CG and Security still want a core BioCompute Provenance example, open or apply a current-build issue that identifies the target artifact and the intended Provenance.agent/Provenance.entity semantics; otherwise leave the removed Sequence/MolecularSequence-era examples out of the current core build.
issue_request: FHIR-11012 was a Published/Persuasive Clinical Genomics DSTU2 issue for FHIR-core-Sequence requesting a Provenance resource example and reference that show how a BioCompute scenario can be recorded.
initial_application: The request was historically applied by #11012 commits including 7adda962ef162603623942f5bcb42a113c34e610 and 8c08a289ecb021510117a3d3f0c9f353594c1e57, which added BioCompute and CWL Provenance examples and list entries. Later maintenance updated their targets from Sequence/MolecularSequence to MolecularDefinition before the examples were deleted during MolecularSequence cleanup.
additional_context: Current fhir.ini lists Sequence under removed resources and comments out MolecularSequence while keeping Provenance active; the current source contains no BioCompute/CWL Provenance examples. FHIR-51227 records the R6 CG decision replacing MolecularSequence with MolecularDefinition. FHIR-50994 and Security WG minutes later questioned whether the BioCompute object in the removed example should be modeled as Provenance.entity or as a software/device agent, and FHIR-50994 was retracted/no-change without approving a replacement example.
reconciliation: No source change was made. Reintroducing the old example would require choosing a new current-build target artifact and deciding whether BioCompute is an input entity, an agent/device, or both, which is a new modeling decision rather than a safe mechanical restoration of the applied Sequence-era issue.

related_jiras.note: R6 decision replacing MolecularSequence with MolecularDefinition; it explains why the old Sequence/MolecularSequence target is not a current core build source target.
Raised the later ambiguity in the BioCompute Provenance example's entity-versus-agent modeling and was retracted/no-change without a replacement decision.

evidence_items.summary: Published/Persuasive Clinical Genomics issue requesting a Provenance example and reference for recording a BioCompute scenario for the Sequence artifact.
evidence_items.learned: The work group request was final and defines the historical change to audit.

evidence_items.summary: The #11012 commits added BioCompute and CWL Provenance examples, including provenance-example-biocompute-object.xml and provenance-example-cwl.xml.
evidence_items.learned: FHIR-11012 was historically applied in the old Sequence-era Provenance example source.

evidence_items.summary: Current build metadata lists Sequence as removed, comments out MolecularSequence, keeps Provenance active, and current source contains no BioCompute or CWL Provenance example entries.
evidence_items.learned: The original target resource is outside current build scope and the old example cannot be restored unchanged.

evidence_items.summary: Applied/Persuasive with Modification R6 issue stating that MolecularDefinition supersedes MolecularSequence and covers its prior use cases.
evidence_items.learned: Later CG decisions intentionally changed the genomics resource model, so a Sequence/MolecularSequence example rewrite would be a new modeling decision.

evidence_items.summary: Resolved-No-Change/Retracted issue observing that the BioCompute Provenance example title implied an agent while the example modeled BioCompute as an entity.
evidence_items.learned: The old example had a substantive modeling ambiguity and no final replacement source change was approved in that issue.

evidence_items.summary: Security WG minutes discussed FHIR-50994 and asked whether the BioCompute example should describe a practitioner using BioCompute as input or a BioCompute system acting as the source/agent.
evidence_items.learned: Community minutes support treating the example semantics as unresolved enough to require human review.

evidence_items.summary: Current Provenance guidance models automata that create resources as Provenance.agent and original content as Provenance.entity.
evidence_items.learned: Choosing how to model BioCompute in a replacement example is a substantive Provenance design choice.
